headline: Grasses are the most successful plants on Earth—feeding billions and shaping continents
universal_truth: The humble and overlooked often have the greatest impact
fun_facts: Grasses cover 40% of Earth's land surface—more than any other plant family
Every major civilization was built on grass: wheat, rice, corn, and barley are all grasses
Grass grows from the base, not the tip—that's why mowing doesn't kill it
discussion_questions: What humble things in your life have the biggest impact?
Why do we overlook things that are everywhere?
What would the world look like without grass?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: It's everywhere. You walk on it, ignore it, mow it down—and it grows right back. Grass seems ordinary. But this humble plant feeds most of humanity, shapes entire ecosystems, and covers more of Earth than any other plant family. Never underestimate grass.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Why is grass so incredibly successful? Trees are taller. Flowers are prettier. Yet grass conquered 40% of Earth's land surface. What's the secret behind this global domination?

options.text: It grows from the base, survives grazing and fire, and spreads aggressively
options.response: Yes. Grass evolved to thrive on disturbance—fire, grazing, and mowing only make it stronger.

options.text: It needs less water and nutrients than other plants
options.response: Some grasses are hardy, but the real secret is in how they grow...

q1.title: Civilization's Foundation
q1.script: Wheat, rice, corn, barley, oats, millet, sugarcane—all grasses. Every major civilization was built on domesticated grass. The calories that fuel humanity come overwhelmingly from this one plant family. Grass is the foundation of human history.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Civilization's Foundation"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Invincible Design
q2.script: Most plants grow from the tip—cut the tip, kill the plant. Grass grows from the base. Mow it, graze it, burn it—the growth point survives underground. This simple adaptation lets grass thrive where other plants would die.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Grassland Power
q3.script: Grasslands store massive amounts of carbon in their roots—sometimes more than forests. The American prairies had roots 15 feet deep. Grasslands also prevent erosion, filter water, and support countless species. The invisible half of grass may be the most important.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: The most impactful things are often the most overlooked. Grass teaches us that success isn't about being the biggest or flashiest—it's about resilience, adaptation, and showing up everywhere, consistently.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 61—welcome to March's Life Science theme! Tomorrow, we'll discover why wetlands matter. Until then, notice the grass around you—it's quietly running the world.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Hidden Impact - Honor the Overlooked
growTrack.learning_objective: Recognize the outsized impact of humble, consistent things
growTrack.activity: Identify something in your life that's 'grass-like'—humble, overlooked, but essential. Maybe a daily habit, a person who quietly supports you, or a routine you take for granted. Acknowledge its importance today.
